note: Hand-authored for spec 09 step 1. Every expected value is independent arithmetic, an Excel fact (=1/0 is #DIV/0!, NA() is #N/A, the 1900 date serial) or a stated contract rule; none is copied from an engine run. Reports omit `engine`.
comparison: Every calculation-report.v2 field except `engine` is compared. Two integers (revisions, counts, now_ms, utc_offset_minutes) are equal only when they are the same integer. Any other pair of numbers is equal when |actual - expected| <= numeric_tolerance * max(1, |expected|); a calculated value is a binary64 number even where this file writes it without a fraction. An error value is compared on `error` only. Diagnostics are compared in order on (code, sheet, address), and each actual `message` must be a non-empty string. Everything else is exact, including list order. In a document's `open` block, conversion `present` means only that the conversion is not null. A source_fingerprint is a literal: `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the exact bytes the test passes to open, taken with `shasum -a 256` and not from a session. Those bytes are the document_fixture file, or the UTF-8 bytes of the document's document_text, which is the same document as its `document` member written as one line of JSON text.

derivation.now: The pinned now_ms 1767225600000 is 20454 * 86400000, exactly 20454 days after 1970-01-01, whose 1900-system serial is 25569; with a zero offset NOW() is 25569 + 20454 = 46023.
derivation.formula_counts: calculated_formulas and unresolved_formulas range over the formula cells in the pass's closure: every formula cell when no outputs are bound, otherwise the formula cells the bound outputs depend on. calculated_formulas counts those with a key in values, unresolved_formulas those without. Each document's formula_counts member works its two numbers out by hand from its bound outputs.
derivation.evaluated_cells: A pass with no base (base_revision null) runs every formula cell in the closure that is free of a structural error. A pass with a base runs the cells downstream of the inputs changed since that base: unit_price reaches C2:C4, E2:E4, F2, F3, F4 (9); unit_cost and fixed_cost together reach D2:D4, E2:E4, F3, F4 (8). Forecast!J1 is volatile and runs on every pass; Forecast!F5 has no precedent and runs only on a full pass; Forecast!J2 does not parse and never runs. A preview runs on a detached copy with no published report, so its `before` pass is full.
derivation.origin: inputs[].origin is null until this session (or the session a preview was forked from) has applied that input, then `authored`.
derivation.diagnostic_code: parse_error is the documented engine code for a formula that does not parse (docs/refusal-codes.md).

planner.formula_counts: Bound outputs are Forecast!F2, F3 and F4. F2 = SUM(C2:C4) reaches C2, C3, C4. F3 = SUM(E2:E4) reaches E2, E3, E4, and each E row reads its C and D, so D2, D3, D4 join. F4 reads only the three Assumptions values. Closure formula cells: C2:C4 (3) + D2:D4 (3) + E2:E4 (3) + F2, F3, F4 (3) = 12, which is every formula cell in the document. All 12 have a value in every state, so calculated_formulas is 12 and unresolved_formulas is 0.

canonical.formula_counts: Bound outputs are Forecast!F2, F3, F4, F5, J1 and J2. F2, F3 and F4 reach the same 12 formula cells as the planner document. F5 (=1/0), J1 (=NOW()) and J2 (=1+) are bound outputs themselves and read no other cell. Closure formula cells: 12 + 3 = 15, which is every formula cell in the file. J2 does not parse, so it has no key in values; the other 14 do (an error value such as #DIV/0! or #N/A is a value). calculated_formulas is 14 and unresolved_formulas is 1.

legacy_revision.formula_counts: The bound output is S!A3 (=A1+A2), the only formula cell; it reads two plain values. Closure formula cells: 1. It has a value, so calculated_formulas is 1 and unresolved_formulas is 0.

cache.formula_counts: Bound outputs are S!A1 (=1+1) and S!B1 (=1+); neither reads another cell. Closure formula cells: 2. A1 has a value (2) and B1 does not parse, so calculated_formulas is 1 and unresolved_formulas is 1.

partial.formula_counts: The document has three formula cells: S!A3 (=A1+A2), S!B1 (=A1*10) and S!B2 (=1+, which does not parse). Bound outputs are S!A1 and S!A2, which are plain values, and S!A3, which reads A1 and A2. The closure is therefore A1, A2 and A3, and its only formula cell is A3. B1 and B2 are formula cells no bound output depends on: they are outside the closure, so they are absent from values and evaluated_cells, B2 gets no parse_error diagnostic, and neither is counted. A3 has a value on every pass, so calculated_formulas is 1 and unresolved_formulas is 0. Counted over the whole workbook instead, the numbers would be 2 and 1.
partial.outputs_on_plain_cells: echo is bound to the input cell S!A1 and fixed to the literal S!A2. Neither is a formula, so each takes its origin as an input does and its result is the cell's value: both origins are null and the results 1 and 2 before any write; after the session sets a = 10, echo is `authored` with result 10 and fixed is unchanged. sum = A1 + A2 is 1 + 2 = 3, then 10 + 2 = 12.

open_refusals.note: Documents that CalculationSession.open refuses, with the code each engine reports (the session contract, section 4, reader codes). `document` is text; the test passes its UTF-8 bytes to open with no input_kinds. Bytes that are not JSON and a root that is not an object are refused by open itself as invalid_model in both languages, before a reader is chosen. A JSON object goes to the toolkit reader, and the two readers do not share every code: the Rust reader deserialises into typed structs and a document it cannot deserialise has no code of its own, so open reports it as invalid_model, while the Python reader reports the code of the first rule it finds broken. The cases where the two columns differ are those reader differences; the test also checks that they are exactly the ones named in `reader_differences`.

cases.name: byte-order-mark
cases.reason: A byte order mark is not JSON.

cases.name: nan-constant
cases.reason: NaN is not a JSON value.

cases.name: array-root
cases.reason: The root is not an object. The second element must not be read as a positional revision.

cases.name: null-root
cases.reason: The root is not an object.

cases.name: no-version
cases.reason: A document with no schema_version is not a version 1 document (docs/specs/model-versioning.md).

cases.name: empty-object
cases.reason: Reader difference. Python checks the version before anything else; the Rust struct reader cannot build a document without `sheets` and has no code of its own.

cases.name: fractional-version
cases.reason: Reader difference. Python reports the version rule; the Rust struct reader cannot read 1.0 as an integer and has no code of its own.

cases.name: list-cell-value
cases.reason: Reader difference. Python reports the cell-value rule; the Rust struct reader cannot read a list as a cell value and has no code of its own.

revision_key.note: template is JSON text; a test splices each accept or refuse entry in place of @, so large and fractional numbers survive exactly. Every reader of a v1 toolkit document accepts each accept spelling and the absent form, and refuses each refuse spelling. opens_at is the revision of a calculation session opened on an accepted document: the session contract starts it at 0 and reports the dropped key. An engine session built from the same text is seeded by the key; that rule is tested outside this table. reader_differences lists the spellings the two JSON readers do not treat alike; both are general JSON-reader differences, not revision logic.

reader_differences.name: negative-zero
reader_differences.reason: Python's JSON reader parses -0 as the integer 0; Rust's parses -0 as a float, which is not an unsigned integer.

reader_differences.name: duplicate-key
reader_differences.reason: Python's JSON reader keeps the last of two members with the same name; Rust's derived reader refuses a duplicate field.
